title: 89. Koko Eating Bananas

examples.explanation: At 4 bananas/hour Koko takes ceil(3/4)+ceil(6/4)+ceil(7/4)+ceil(11/4) = 1+2+2+3 = 8 hours; at 3 bananas/hour she would take 1+2+3+4 = 10 hours, exceeding the 8-hour limit.
At 30 bananas/hour Koko takes ceil(30/30)+ceil(11/30)+ceil(23/30)+ceil(4/30)+ceil(20/30) = 1+1+1+1+1 = 5 hours; at 29 bananas/hour she would take 2+1+1+1+1 = 6 hours, exceeding the 5-hour limit.
At 23 bananas/hour Koko takes ceil(30/23)+ceil(11/23)+ceil(23/23)+ceil(4/23)+ceil(20/23) = 2+1+1+1+1 = 6 hours; at 22 bananas/hour she would take 2+1+2+1+1 = 7 hours, exceeding the 6-hour limit.

hints: For a fixed speed k, one pile of size p takes ceil(p / k) hours.
If a speed is fast enough, every larger speed is also fast enough.
Binary-search speeds from 1 through the largest pile and accumulate hours in a wide integer type.
